dedupe_keys.name: wisconsin dnr groundwater and environmental monitoring system gems landfill groundwater leachate and gas monitoring data

description: GEMS is the Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources' database of environmental monitoring data from licensed landfills, collected since the mid-1970s and used by programme staff to evaluate landfill performance, environmental impacts and the effectiveness of remedial actions. It holds results from more than 600 landfills: analyses of groundwater from monitoring wells and nearby private drinking water wells, leachate, surface water and air, methane gas readings from gas probes and extraction wells, and water table measurements, plus data from a few hazardous waste facilities. Some older sites have records back to the late 1970s. Coverage is Wisconsin. Facilities and consultants submit the data to the DNR, and the records are public, available from the DNR. Caveats: sampling frequency and parameters differ between sites and decades, older data may be less reliable, and the database is designed for regulatory review, not research, so extracts need cleaning. Simulation uses: long time series for calibrating landfill leachate and gas generation models, assessing groundwater contamination risk around waste sites, and studying landfill behaviour under changing climate. Related records: the IPCC Waste Model (model-ipcc-waste-model-first-order-decay) and the CARB Landfill Gas Tool (model-carb-landfill-gas-tool) need such monitoring data for calibration.
